title: Fingerprints of Excitonic Collective Modes in the Two-Dimensional Electron Gas
authors: Jakob Wolff, Silvana Botti, Lucia Reining, Matteo Gatti
abstract: The two-dimensional homogeneous electron gas (2D HEG) is a prototype system of fundamental interest that can be realized experimentally over a wide range of densities. Here, we investigate its collective charge excitations at low densities, using time-dependent density functional theory. We demonstrate that, beyond traditional plasmons, new collective excitonic modes emerge for a Wigner-Seitz radius larger than $r_{\mathrm s} \approx 1$. These excitonic modes leave characteristic fingerprints in experimentally accessible quantities, namely, asymmetric peak structures in the loss function and very strong Friedel-like oscillations in the static linear density response that increase when the system approaches a regime of instability. Indeed, at low enough densities the collective modes cross the zero energy axis, indicating an instability of the paramagnetic 2D HEG towards the formation of a charge-density-wave phase with excitonic origin. These findings provide valuable insights for the experimental detection of excitonic collective modes in tunable 2D electron systems and contribute to the fundamental understanding of many-body effects in low-density electron gases.
summary: This work uses TDDFT to explore collective charge excitations in the 2DEG, finding that excitonic modes appear at low densities, distinct from simple plasmons. The theory predicts that these modes signal an instability towards a charge-density-wave phase when the electron density drops sufficiently low. The findings offer concrete, measurable fingerprints for experimental detection in tunable 2D electron systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the existence and experimental signatures of excitonic collective charge excitations in the Two-Dimensional Electron Gas (2DEG) at low densities.
main_result: New excitonic modes emerge beyond traditional plasmons at low densities, and the system is predicted to become unstable towards a charge-density-wave (CDW) phase when the Wigner-Seitz radius exceeds a critical value.
method: The research employs Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (TDDFT) within the framework of the Casida equation, comparing results across various approximations for the exchange-correlation (xc) kernel.
model_or_system: The physical system is the two-dimensional homogeneous electron gas (2D HEG), a model system whose properties are tunable by varying the electron density via the Wigner-Seitz radius ($r_s$).
key_observables: Loss function ($	ext{Im} \epsilon^{-1}(q, \omega)$), static linear density response ($\chi(q, \omega=0)$), and induced density oscillations ($\Delta n(r)$).
important_parameters: Wigner-Seitz radius ($r_s$), wavevector ($q$), and frequency ($\omega$). The critical instability is predicted around $r_s \gtrsim 14.455$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations for the xc kernel, comparing RPA, ALDA, DPGT, and DPGT+NCT, with the most detailed results using the DPGT+NCT parametrization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the development of asymmetric peak structures in the loss function and strong Friedel-like oscillations in the static response function as $r_s$ increases, particularly near $q=2k_F$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the predictions of various theoretical approximations (RPA vs. DPGT+NCT) for collective excitations, focusing on how excitonic effects manifest in the loss function and the static density response, culminating in the prediction of a CDW instability.
why_interesting: The detailed study of collective excitations and instability mechanisms in a fundamental model system like the 2DEG provides crucial theoretical benchmarks for understanding strongly correlated electron behavior in low-dimensional materials.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Loss functions for (a) rs = 5 and (b)-(d) rs = 14, obtained using (a)-(b) the DPGT+NCT (see text), (c) the DPGT, and (d) the ALDA xc kernels. The collective modes ωc(q) are depicted by solid white lines, while the RPA plasmon is shown by light grey dots. The lines stop when the collective modes cease to exist. The black dashed line denotes the maximum of the loss function. In panel (a) and (b), the dashed line terminates because the loss function develops a double-peak structure, and the high energy peak around ω/EF ≈25 becomes more intense than the lower-energy structure.

Figure 2. Loss functions at q = 2kF. The DPGT+NCT loss functions for different rs are shown by colored solid lines. The DPGT as well as the RPA loss functions are shown for rs = 14 and represented by a solid and dashed black line, respectively. In the RPA, almost all spectral weight is in the plasmon peak, while the DPGT(+NCT) spectra develop asymmetric peaks inside the particle-hole continuum.

Figure 3. Electron-hole correlation function: electron distri- bution around a hole at the origin, for a wavevector q in y direction and rs = 14. Upper panels: RPA. Lower panels: DPGT+NCT. The left panel, for q = 0.5kF, shows the plas- mon. The next two panels show results for wavevector and energy where the collective mode in DPGT+NCT is inside the continuum and close to its left border, or close to the minimum of the mode dispersion, respectively. The intensi- ties in all panels are normalized to their respective maximum. For DPGT and ALDA see [104] Fig. S3.
